clues: This town is the most peopled town of its shire, in the north-east of its land. It stands on a small river that feeds a more great one.
Though sea winds soften its air, this town's inland spot leaves it prone to sharp heats and colds. Low clouds rule much of its year.
In 496 a Frankish king was washed in this town's great church. That rite made the church the crown place of kings for ages.
Folk call this the Town of Crownings. King on king was crowned in its great church through the long ages of the realm.
This town lies on the north edge of the land of the famed fizz wine. Its name is bound to that wine's making and its sale to the world.
